question.problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ -14 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
question.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -20 \\ 0 & 2 & -14 \\ -1 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -20 \\ 0 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 4 & k-20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -20 \\ 0 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & k+8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-20 \\ 2{x}_{2}=-14 \\ 0=k+8.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k+8,$ which means that $k=-8.$
